name: Nigerian Pepper Soup
summary: A thin, fiery broth scented with calabash nutmeg and uda, cooked with goat meat, chicken or catfish.
story: Pepper soup is a light, intensely spiced broth enjoyed across Nigeria, often served at gatherings, in bars and as a comforting dish when someone has a cold. It is made with goat, chicken, fish or offal, and spice mixes vary by region. It is usually eaten as a soup by itself, sometimes with boiled yam.

steps.title: Season the meat
steps.text: Wash the meat and put it in a pot with the onion, ginger, garlic, a stock cube and salt. Cover and steam on low heat for 10 minutes until the meat releases its juices.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Pour in the water and bring to a boil, skimming off any grey foam that rises to the surface.

steps.title: Cook until tender
steps.text: Simmer covered until the meat is tender: goat takes about 40 minutes, chicken 20 minutes. A knife should slide in easily.

steps.title: Add the spice
steps.text: Stir in the pepper soup spice mix and blended scotch bonnet. Simmer for 10 minutes until the aroma is strong and peppery.

steps.title: Add leaves
steps.text: Drop in the scent leaves and cook for 2 minutes, just until wilted and fragrant.

steps.title: Taste and serve
steps.text: Adjust salt and pepper. Serve very hot in bowls with the broth, which should be thin, clear-ish and slightly oily.

tips: Toast whole spices lightly before grinding to deepen the flavour.
Add the spice mix after the meat is tender so it does not turn bitter from long cooking.
For catfish, add the fish only for the last 10 to 12 minutes to keep it intact.

swaps.swap: Ready-made Nigerian pepper soup spice from African shops. In a pinch, use black pepper, ground cloves, nutmeg and a pinch of ground coriander; the taste will be different.
Fresh basil or a mix of basil and mint.
